      "displayName": "Protein Types Distribution with Percentages Chart",
      "queryLines": [
        "-- What types of proteins does this dataset contain? What is their corresponding percentage relative to the existing data and provide a chart for the output.\n",
        "SELECT\n",
        "  label,\n",
        "  COUNT(*) AS count,\n",
        "  ROUND((COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER()), 2) AS percentage\n",
        "FROM\n",
        "  demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.proteinclassification_tiny\n",
        "GROUP BY\n",
        "  label"
      ]
    },

      "queryLines": [
        "SELECT\n",

        "  o.Organism_SimpleTerm,\n",
        "  o.Organism_Definition,\n",
        "  p.label,\n",
        "  COUNT(DISTINCT p.ProteinName) AS Protein_Count,\n",
        "  collect_set(p.ProteinName) AS Distinct_Protein_Names,\n",
        "  o.SimpleTermDict \n",
        "FROM\n",
        "  demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.proteinclassification_tiny p\n",
        "JOIN\n",
        "  demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.tinysample_organism_info_scientificnsimple o \n",
        "  ON p.OrganismName = o.OrganismName\n",
        "WHERE\n",
        "  p.score > 0.85\n",
        "GROUP BY\n",
        "  p.OrganismName,\n",
        "  o.SimpleTermDict,\n",
        "  p.label,\n",
        "  o.Organism_SimpleTerm,\n",
        "  o.Organism_Definition\n",

        "  -- p.label\n",

        "  COUNT(DISTINCT o.SimpleTermDict) > 1\n",
        "ORDER BY\n",
        "  TypeCount DESC"

      "displayName": "Membrane/Soluble Protein Research Insights and Drug Discovery Potential",
      "queryLines": [
        "SELECT\n",
        "  OrganismName,\n",
        "  Organism_SimpleTerm,\n",
        "  ProteinName,\n",
        "  -- ai_query(\n",
        "  --   'az_openai_gpt4o', -- deployed external endpoint on e2-demo-west-ws\n",
        "  --   CONCAT('You are well-versed in membrane proteins and drug discovery research. Please be brief. Provide a dictionary of responses in the format {\"key\": \"response\"} to the following keys \"information\", \"recent_research\" and highlight \"under_researched_areas\" that hold promise for drug discovery for the given \"protein name\": ', ProteinName, ' Output just the dictionary {\"information\": \"response\", \"recent_research\": \"response\", \"under_researched_areas\": \"response\"}. Do not include \"```json\" strings in output')\n",
        "  -- ) AS researchDict,\n",
        "  demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.get_protein_research_info(ProteinName) AS researchDict, -- using the registered SQL_function here\n",
        "  GET_JSON_OBJECT(researchDict, '$.information') AS information,\n",
        "  GET_JSON_OBJECT(researchDict, '$.recent_research') AS recent_research,\n",
        "  GET_JSON_OBJECT(researchDict, '$.under_researched_areas') AS under_researched_areas,\n",
        "  ProteinType,\n",
        "  ProteinClassificationScore\n",
        "\n",
        "FROM \n",
        "(\n",
        "  SELECT\n",
        "    p.ProteinName,\n",
        "    p.label AS ProteinType,\n",
        "    p.score AS ProteinClassificationScore,\n",
        "    p.GeneName,\n",
        "    p.Sequence,\n",
        "    p.Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "    p.OrganismName,\n",
        "    o.Organism_SimpleTerm\n",
        "\n",
        "  FROM\n",
        "    demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.proteinclassification_tiny p\n",
        "    JOIN demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.tinysample_organism_info_scientificNsimple o ON p.OrganismName = o.OrganismName\n",
        "\n",
        "-- Takes a while to process -- so we will use all values and filter instead except for the p.score/ProteinClassificationScore\n",
        "\n",
        "--   WHERE\n",
        "--     p.score > 0.85\n",
        "--   AND\n",
        "--     o.Organism_SimpleTerm ILIKE '%human%'\n",
        "-- );\n",
        "\n",
        "   WHERE \n",
        "      p.score > :ProteinClassificationScore \n",
        "   AND \n",
        "      o.Organism_SimpleTerm ILIKE '%' || :Organism_SimpleTerm || '%'\n",
        "      -- (:Organism_SimpleTerm = '*' OR o.Organism_SimpleTerm ILIKE '%' || COALESCE(:Organism_SimpleTerm, '') || '%')   \n",
        ");"

    {
      "name": "64cd72e9",
      "displayName": "Human vs Frog Summary Statistics",
      "queryLines": [
        "SELECT \n",
        "  o.Organism_SimpleTerm,\n",
        "  p.label AS ProteinType,\n",
        "  COUNT(DISTINCT p.ProteinName) AS Protein_Count,\n",
        "  ROUND(AVG(p.Molecular_Weight), 2) AS Avg_Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "  ROUND(MIN(p.Molecular_Weight), 2) AS Min_Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "  ROUND(MAX(p.Molecular_Weight), 2) AS Max_Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "  ROUND(AVG(p.score), 3) AS Avg_Classification_Score\n",
        "FROM demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.proteinclassification_tiny p\n",
        "JOIN demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.tinysample_organism_info_scientificnsimple o \n",
        "  ON p.OrganismName = o.OrganismName\n",
        "WHERE o.Organism_SimpleTerm IN ('Human', 'African clawed frog', 'Western clawed frog')\n",
        "GROUP BY o.Organism_SimpleTerm, p.label\n",

    {

      "displayName": "Human vs Bacteria Summary Statistics",

        "  ROUND(MIN(p.Molecular_Weight), 2) AS Min_Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "  ROUND(MAX(p.Molecular_Weight), 2) AS Max_Molecular_Weight,\n",
        "  ROUND(AVG(p.score), 3) AS Avg_Classification_Score\n",
        "FROM demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.proteinclassification_tiny p\n",
        "JOIN demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery.tinysample_organism_info_scientificnsimple o \n",
        "  ON p.OrganismName = o.OrganismName\n",
        "WHERE o.Organism_SimpleTerm = 'Human' \n",
        "   OR o.Organism_SimpleTerm LIKE '%bacteria%' \n",
        "   OR o.Organism_SimpleTerm LIKE '%Bacteria%'\n",
        "GROUP BY \n",
        "  CASE \n",
        "    WHEN o.Organism_SimpleTerm = 'Human' THEN 'Human'\n",
        "    ELSE 'Bacteria'\n",
        "  END,\n",
        "  p.label\n",
        "ORDER BY Organism_Category, p.label"
      ]
    }

              "lines": [
                "# AI-Driven Drug Discovery\n",
                "Protein Classification Data Exploration AI/BI Genie Space  with GenAI-backed AI-Queries to Help Focus Downstream Drug Discovery Efforts   \n",
                "      \n",
                "#### OVERVIEW: \n",
                "The Life Sciences and Pharmaceutical research and development cycle — which encompasses the discovery, preclinical testing, and early clinical trial phases — is notoriously lengthy, spanning on average ~10-15 years, with a significant portion of drug candidates failing during clinical trials. It is anticipated that the use of Generative AI (GenAI) and Transformer Models will help expedite this process, e.g., by analyzing vast datasets to identify promising drug candidates, predict their efficacy, and optimize molecular structures, leading to faster identification of potential drugs and reducing the time and cost of development. ([ref](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/life-sciences/our-insights/generative-ai-in-the-pharmaceutical-industry-moving-from-hype-to-reality#/))\n",
                "\n",
                "#### GOAL: \n",
                "**We provide an example of how GenAI can be leveraged to discover more about protein properties and whether there are candidate proteins that are under-researched in areas that show promise for potential drug discovery**.   \n",
                "This [AI/BI Dashboard](https://docs.databricks.com/en/dashboards/index.html) and the [enabled](https://docs.databricks.com/en/dashboards/index.html#enable-a-genie-space-from-your-dashboard) [Genie Space](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01efc9fc59e2146eab09fc4e6a4b9a5a) allows you to explore the corresponding protein datasets and \"***Ask Genie***\" (*see dashboard top-left-corner*). You can also refer to [additional Example Queries](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1625373258643555?o=2556758628403379) to *Ask Genie*.\n",
                "\n",
                "\n",
                "#### [DATA & PROCESSING](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/browse/folders/4420661094443359?o=2556758628403379): \n",
                "\n",
                "To make sense of the *alphabet soup* in our sample of protein sequences, we derive `proteinclassification_tiny`, which contains various columns related to *protein* `classification` (with corresponding `labels` and `scores` as well as protein information), by   \n",
                "   - i) pre-processing the [FASTA protein sequence data](https://www.uniprot.org/help/downloads) using a [Protein Data Processing](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/pipelines/00b4ca96-c5b4-470a-937f-14cb2660ff90/updates/0977eef3-490a-4eac-8a31-ee128fff8d62?o=2556758628403379) [Delta Live Tables](https://www.databricks.com/product/delta-live-tables) pipeline to help extract protein information e.g. *identifiers*, *sequences*, *names*, *organism information*, *gene names*, *protein existence*, and *molecular weight*;    \n",
                "   - ii) perform **[protein sequence classification](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/3667893373920805?o=2556758628403379)** using [a hybrid approach that combines Protein Language Model, e.g., ProtBERT-BFD and a Classifier, e.g., CNN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37497772/) to provide enhanced identification of [`membrane transport proteins`](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-17216-1) (cf. `water soluble` proteins). We can then sift out protein classification at a suitably high (adjustable) classification confidence threshold      \n",
                "---        \n",
                "Additional post-processing with GenAI in [`ai-query()`](https://docs.databricks.com/en/sql/language-manual/functions/ai_query.html) yielded the following 2 datasets, which can potentially help in downstream drug discovery processes.\n",
                "   - `tinysample_organism_info_scientificNsimple`: contains scientific (`OrganismName`), layman (`Organism_SimpleTerm`), and corresponding `Organism_Definition` information about the different organisms found in the `proteinclassification_tiny` table. It is derived with [ai_query](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1625373258635024?o=2556758628403379#command/1625373258638832) using the pay-per-token [Foundational Model API](https://docs.databricks.com/en/machine-learning/foundation-models/index.html) `databricks-meta-llama-3-1-70b-instruct` [model endpoint](https://docs.databricks.com/en/machine-learning/model-serving/index.html) and making [batch interferencing](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1625373258635024?o=2556758628403379#command/1625373258638913) with the `ai_query()` registered as a [User Defined Function in Unity Catalog](https://docs.databricks.com/en/udf/unity-catalog.html).     \n",
                "---\n",
                "   - `tinysample_organism_protein_research_info`: contains research information about organisms and their associated proteins, including `recent research` and `under-researched areas` of these proteins that show potential promise for drug discovery. These research insights are derived with the help of [using `Azure OpenAI GPT-4o` served as an External Model Endpoint](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1625373258636712?o=2556758628403379) and [queried as an External Model using `ai-query()`](https://docs.databricks.com/en/large-language-models/ai-query-external-model.html). For more efficient exploration, the queries for our `tinysample` of proteins are [preprocessed in bulk](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1625373258636712?o=2556758628403379%3Fparent%3Dfolders%2F1625373258638091#command/1625373258641291).      \n",
                "\n",
                "These tables are found within the demo workspace [Unity Catalog](https://docs.databricks.com/en/catalogs/index.html) and [Schema](https://docs.databricks.com/en/schemas/index.html#what-is-a-schema): [`demos_genie.hls_ai_drug_discovery`](https://e2-demo-west.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/demos_genie/hls_ai_drug_discovery?o=2556758628403379) and are connected primarily through the `OrganismName`.        \n",
                "\n",
                "The following diagram illustrates the flow of processes involved and the [Databricks Intelligent Platform](https://www.databricks.com/resources/demos/tours/horizontal/introducing-databricks-intelligence-platform) features utilized (in red):    \n",

                "---   \n",
                "\n",

                "\n",
                "#### DOWNSTREAM EXAMPLE USE CASE : \n",
                "- In section section `3.1` we provide an example of how we can leverage GenAI models (that were trained with real-world research knowledge or fine-tuned to research-relevant publications, e.g., [OpenAI-GPT-4o]((https://openai.com/index/gpt-4o-system-card/) ) to help us to zoom in on under-researched areas for those membrane/soluble proteins that were confidently classified and further investigate their potential therapeutic candidacy. \n",
                "\n",
                "#### FUTURE USE CASE:\n",
                "We envision being able to pick candidate proteins to visualize their 3D structure and explore their properties interactively, all on our Data Intelligence Platform. The hope is to use Deep Learning models (e.g., [AlphaFold](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-03819-2), [RFdiffusion](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06415-8), including other relevant Life Sciences GenAI/Transformer models, etc.) trained or fine-tuned to predict protein function and structure ([ref](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphafold-reveals-the-structure-of-the-protein-universe/)), and potentially simulate new proteins or ways to interact with protein properties ([ref](https://www.ipd.uw.edu/software/)) *in silico* ([ref](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07601-y)).  To this end, a *work-in-progress* endeavor by the HLS SSA team is to develop capabilities around `Protein Folding` and a suite of discovery tools within `Genesis WorkBench` for Life Sciences R&D. "
